34:1: God Almighty says: All thanks and all praise are due to the One Who is worshipped, Who is the Owner of everything in the seven heavens and the seven earths, apart from everything that they worship and apart from everything else. There is no Owner of any of that other than Him. So the meaning is: He Who is the Owner of all of it, And to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter. He says: All thanks are due to Him in the Hereafter, just as that is due to Him in this immediate world, because from Him are all blessings upon everyone in the heavens and the earth in this world, and from Him will be that in the Hereafter. So all praise is due to God alone, apart from anything else in this immediate world and the hereafter, because all blessings are from Him, and no one shares them with Him besides Him. He is the Wise in His management of His creation and His dispensing of them according to His decree. He is aware of them and what is good for them, and of what they have done and what they will do. He encompasses all of that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And He is the Wise, the All-Aware. Wise in His affair, All-Aware of His creation.
34:2: God Almighty says: He knows what enters the earth and what disappears from it, from their saying: I entered such-and-such: if I entered it, as the poet said: I saw the rhymes swaying in a melodious manner, and it was difficult for needles to insert them. What he means by his saying: They enter into entrances: They enter entrances. And what comes out of it means: And what comes out of the earth. And what descends from the sky and what ascends therein means: And what ascends in the sky. This is report from God that He is the All-Knowing from whom nothing is hidden in the heavens and the earth, of what is apparent in them and what is hidden. He is the Most Merciful, the Most Forgiving. He is the Most Merciful to the people of repentance among His servants, that He does not punish them after their repentance. He is the Forgiver of their sins if they repent from them.
34:3: God the Most High says: And those of your people who denied God's ability to recreate Him after their annihilation in the form they were in before their annihilation urge you, O Muhammad, to hasten the coming of the Hour, mocking your promise to them and denying your report. Say to them: Yes, by my Lord, it will come to you. I swear by Him that the Hour will come to you. Then He, the Most High, returned after mentioning the Hour to Himself and glorifying it, and said, Knower of the unseen. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it ‘Alim al-Ghaib’ in the nominative case as a resumption, since there was a barrier between His statement and my Lord and His statement the Knower of the Unseen. Some of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as ‘Alim’ in the fa’il form, but they lowered ‘Alim’ in response to His statement and my Lord as it was a description of Him. The rest of the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as ‘Alam al-Ghaib in the fa’il form, and in the genitive case, they responded to its i’rab as it was a description of Him. The correct thing to say about this, according to us, is that all of these three readings are well-known readings among the reciters of the regions and have similar meanings, so whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct. However, the most amazing reading in this regard is that I read with it ‘Alam al-Ghaib in accordance with the reading that I mentioned from the majority of the reciters of the people of Kufa. As for choosing ‘Alam over ‘Aalam, it is because it is more expressive in praising. As for the genitive case in it, it is because it is an attribute of the Lord, and it is in the accusative case. What He meant by His saying Knower of the Unseen is the Knower of what is hidden from the sight of creation, so that no one sees it, either what He did not create from what He will create, or what He created and no one but Him was informed of it. Rather, He, may His praise be glorified, described Himself in this place with His knowledge of the unseen, informing His creation that no one knows the time of the Hour except Him, even if it is coming. So He said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to those who disbelieve in their Lord: Yes, by your Lord, the Hour will surely come to you. But no one knows the time of its coming except the Knower of the Unseen, from whom not an atom’s weight is hidden. What He, the Most High, means by His saying, It is not hidden from Him, is that it is not absent from Him, but it is apparent to Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, It is not hidden from Him, he said: It is not absent from Him. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Nothing is hidden from Him, he said: It is not absent. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Not even an atom’s weight escapes Him: meaning, it does not disappear from Him. We have already explained this with supporting evidence in what has preceded, so there is no need to repeat it here. And His statement, the weight of an atom means: the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth. God Almighty says: Nothing, the weight of an atom or greater or lesser, is hidden from Him, wherever it is in the heavens or on the earth. Nor less than that means: Nothing smaller than the weight of an atom or greater than that is hidden from Him, except in a clear book means: It is established in a book that makes clear to the one looking at it that God Almighty has established it, counted it, and known it, so nothing is hidden from His knowledge.
34:4: God Almighty says: He established this in the clear Book, so that those who believed in God and His Messenger, and did what God and His Messenger commanded them to do, and refrained from what He forbade them from, may be established in their obedience to their Lord. For them is forgiveness God Almighty says: For those who believed and did righteous deeds, there is forgiveness from their Lord for their sins. And a generous provision He says: And a pleasant life on the Day of Resurrection in Paradise. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: For them is forgiveness for their sins and generous provision in Paradise.
34:5: God Almighty says: He established this in the Book, so that He may reward the believers with what He has described, and so that He may reward those who strive to defeat Our verses. He says: And so that He may establish those who worked to invalidate Our proofs and arguments, helping them, who think that they can outsmart Us by themselves, so that We cannot overpower them. For them is a punishment. He says: For them is a punishment of the most severe and painful punishment, and by painful He means: painful. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, They strive against Our signs, trying to outsmart them: meaning, they will not be able to outsmart them. For them is a punishment of a painful torment. He said: The torment is the worst of the torment, and the painful is the hurtful. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, And those who strive to frustrate Our verses, he said: Strive to nullify or invalidate them, he said: And they are the polytheists, and he recited, Do not listen to this Qur’an and speak noisily during it that you may overcome (Fussilat 41:26).
34:6: God Almighty says: He established this in a clear Book, that He may reward those who believe and those who strive in Our verses with what has been made clear to them, and that those who have been given knowledge may see. See is in the accusative case in apposition to His statement: rewards, in His statement, that He may reward those who have believed. What is meant by those who have been given knowledge are the Muslims among the People of the Book, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and his peers who had read the books of God that were revealed before the Criterion. So God Almighty said: And that these who have been given knowledge may see by the Book of God, which is the Torah, the Book that has been revealed to you, O Muhammad, from your Lord, that it is the truth. It was said: What is meant by those who were given knowledge are the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth. He said: The companions of Muhammad. His statement, And guides to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, means: And He guides those who follow it and act in accordance with it to the path of God, the Almighty, in His vengeance against His enemies, the Praiseworthy before His creation, so His favors are with them and His blessings are with them. What he means is that the Book that was revealed to Muhammad guides to Islam.
34:7: God Almighty says: And those who disbelieved in God and in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, astonished at His promise to them of resurrection to one another after death, Shall we direct you, O people, to a man who will inform you that when you are torn apart, you will indeed be in a new creation? That is, he will inform you that after you have been scattered across the earth by a calamity and after your fate in the dust as remains, you will return to your state before death, a new creation. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And those who disbelieved said, ‘Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you, when you are dispersed to every fragment?’ That was said by the polytheists of Quraysh and the polytheists among the people, who will inform you, when you are dispersed to every fragment?: when the earth consumes you, and you become dust and bones, and wild beasts and birds tear you apart, that you will indeed be in a new creation. You will be brought to life and resurrected. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in His statement, Shall We direct you to a man... to a new creation, he said: He says, When you are torn apart, and when you have decayed and become bones, dust, and dust, that is, Every one torn apart, indeed you will be in a new creation. He said: He informs you that you, so the kasra of if did not work in informs you in it, but he began with it as an initiation, because the report is report and a statement, so the kasra in if is for the meaning of the narration in His statement, informs you, not its wording, as if it was said: It was said to you, Indeed you will be in a new creation.
34:8: God Almighty says, informing us of what was said by those who disbelieved in Him and denied that He would send some of them to others after death, amazed by the promise He made to them by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you think this one who promises us that after we are all torn apart in a new creation is a lie to God, so you create falsehood against Him and fabricate falsehood against Him? Or is he mad? He says: Or is he crazy and speaks what has no meaning. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: They said, in denial: Does he invent a lie against God? He said: They said: Either he is lying about God, or he is mad, or he is insane. Rather, those who do not believe... the verse. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Then some of them said to one another, Does he invent a lie against God, or is he mad? The man is crazy and speaks what he does not understand. So God said, Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in the punishment and in extreme error. And His statement, Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in torment and far astray, says the Most High: The matter is not as these polytheists said about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they thought that he had fabricated a lie against God, or that he was in heaven. Rather, those among these polytheists who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in God’s torment in the Hereafter, and will stray far from the path of truth and the straight path. For this reason, they say what they say about him. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la told me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: God said, Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in punishment and far error, and He ordered him to swear to them so that they would take heed. He recited, Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did.' At-Taghabun 64:7... the entire verse. He recited, Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.' Saba' 34:3. The alif in the phrase Has he invented something about God was cut off in the cutting and connecting, so it was opened because it is an alif of interrogation. As for the alif that comes after it, which is an alif of ifta'ala, it was dropped because it is a light, extra letter that is dropped in connected speech. Similar to it are: It is the same for them whether I seek forgiveness for them Al-Munafiqun 60:6, I was arrogant with my own hand Sad 75, I chose the daughters Saffat 37:153, and the like. As for the alif of now and those who remember, this one was lengthened, and that one was not, because alan and al-dhakireen were open, so if it had been dropped, there would have been no difference between the question and the report, so the lengthening in them was made a difference between the question and the report, and the alif of the question is open, so they were separated by that, so that is more indicative of the difference than the lengthening.
34:9: God Almighty says: Have these deniers of the Resurrection, those who reject the Resurrection after death, who say to Our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Does he invent a lie against God, or is there madness in him? not looked at what is before them and what is behind them of the heavens and the earth, and knew that wherever they were, My earth and heavens surround them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, so that they would be deterred from their ignorance and refrain from denying Our signs, lest We command the earth to swallow them up, or the heaven to fall upon them completely? For if We will, We will do that to them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Have they not seen what is before them and what is behind them? He said: They look to their right and to their left, how the sky has encompassed them. If We will, We can cause the earth to swallow them up, just as We caused those who were before them to swallow up. Or cause a fragment of the sky to fall upon them, meaning pieces of the sky. And His statement, Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns [to God], the Most High says: Indeed in the heaven and earth encompassing the servants of God is a sign: that is, a sign for every servant who turns [to God]: that is, for every servant who turns to his Lord in repentance, and returns to knowing His Oneness, and acknowledging His Lordship, and recognizing His Oneness, and submitting to His obedience, on the condition that the one who does that is not prevented from doing anything he wants to do, nor is it difficult for him to do anything he wants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back. The one who turns back is the one who repents.
34:10: God Almighty says: And We had certainly given David bounty from Us, and We said to the mountains, ‘Repeat with him.’ Glorify God with him when he glorifies God. Returning among the Arabs means returning, and a man spending the night in his home and with his family. From this, the poet said: Two days, one day of gatherings and clubs, one day of marching to the enemies for retribution Any return. Some of them read it as Obei ma'ah from Ab ya'ub, meaning: deal with him, and that is a reading that I do not permit reading because it is contrary to the reading of the argument. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told me: Abu Kudayna told us, and Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told us: al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Recite with him means: Pray with him. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, O mountains, echo with him, meaning: Glorify with him. Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Ala’i told us: Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman: O mountains, echo with him, meaning: glorify God. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah: O mountains, echo with him. He said: Praise God in the language of Abyssinia. Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me: Fadil told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, O mountains, echo with him, he said: Glorify with him. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, O mountains, echo with him, he said: Glorify God. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: O mountains, echo with him: meaning, glorify with him when he glorifies. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, O mountains, echo with him, he said: Glorify with him. He said: And the birds as well. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, O mountains, echo with Him, that he said: Glorify Him. Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement, O mountains, echo with him, glorify him. And his saying, and the birds. There are two views regarding the accusative case of the bird: One of them is what Ibn Zayd said, that the bird was called as the mountains were called, so it is accusative because it is conjoined to a nominative case, in a way that does not make it appropriate to repeat its nominative case, so it is like a verbal noun in its own right. The other is: a verb with an omitted pronoun that is not indicated by the speech, so the meaning of the speech is: So We said: O mountains, echo with him, and We subjected the birds to him. If it is raised in response to what is in his saying: Glorify the mountains, it is permissible. It is also permissible to raise the bird while it is conjoined to the mountains, even if it is not appropriate to call it with the way the mountains were called, so it is as the poet said. Except, O Amr and Ad-Dahhak, walk, for you have crossed the road’s vineyard. His saying, And We made iron soft for him, mentioned that the iron was in his hand like wet clay, and he could use it in his hand as he wished, without using fire or striking it with iron. Who said that? Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We made iron soft for him means God made iron subservient to him without fire. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Uthma told us: Saeed bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And We made the iron soft for him, he would straighten it with his hand, and not put it in fire, nor strike it with iron.
34:11: And his saying, Make sabaghat, means: We ordered him to make sabaghat, which are complete twin coats of mail. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Make coats of mail, meaning armor. The first to make them was David. Before that, they were only plates. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, Make long coats of mail, he said: The long coats of mail are iron armor. His saying, And measured in the chain, the people of interpretation differed regarding the chain. Some of them said: The chain is the nail of the collar of the armor. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And he measured the chains. He said: He would make them without fire, nor strike them with iron, then he would chain them together. Chains are the nails in the throat. Others said: It is the throat itself. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And measured in the chain, he said: The chain is its ring, meaning the amount of those rings. He said: And the poet said: Al-Masdi narrated it well and humiliated it He said: He said: He expanded it and shaved it well. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: And measure in the chain. By chain, he means: the hole in the armor, so that its collar is plugged. Some of the people of knowledge of Arabic speech said: It is said that a chained armor is: if its collar is nailed, and he cited as evidence for this saying the saying of the poet: And upon them are two chains of narration, which David ruled or the making of the heavy-duty swords followed. It was said: God said to David, And measure out the chains, because there were previously plates. Who said that? Nasr ibn Ali told us: My father told us: Khalid ibn Qays told us, on the authority of Qatada, And measure the number of chains. He said: They were plates, so he ordered that they be chained together into rings. What he meant by his saying, And measure the number of chains is: He measured the nails in the rings of the armor so that it would be of such size that the nail would not become too thick, nor the ring too narrow, so that the ring would break, nor the ring too wide, nor the nails too small and small, so that they would fit neatly in the ring. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And measure the length of the chain, he said: The length of the nails and the rings. Do not hammer the nails so that they become smooth, and do not sharpen them, Muhammad ibn Amr said, and Al-Harith said: so that they become broken. Ali bin Sahl told me: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and measure the chain, he said: Do not make the nail too small and the ring too large, lest it become untidy, and do not make the nail too large and the ring too small, lest the nail break. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, regarding his statement, And measure the chain, he said: Do not make the nail too thick, lest it break the ring, and do not make it too thin, lest it become loose. And His statement, And do righteous deeds, means that God Almighty says: And, O David, you and your family, work in obedience to God. Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do, meaning that God Almighty says: I am Seeing of what you and your followers do, and nothing of it is hidden from Me, and I will reward you and them for all of that.
34:12: The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, And to Solomon was the wind. The majority of reciters in the regions read it as, And to Solomon was the wind, with the wind in the accusative case, meaning: And We gave David a favor from Us, and We subjected the wind to Solomon. Asim read it as, And to Solomon was the wind, in the nominative case with the adjective, since the accusative case was not apparent. The correct reading of this in our view is the accusative, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. And His saying, Its morning is a month, God Almighty says: And We subjected to Solomon the wind, its morning journey until midday is a month’s journey, and its evening journey from midday until night is a month’s journey. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “And to Solomon We subjected the wind: its morning journey was a month’s journey and its evening journey was a month’s journey.” He said: It goes in the morning a month’s journey, and it comes in the evening a month’s journey. He said: It goes in the morning a month’s journey and it comes in the evening a month’s journey. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: And to Solomon We subjected the wind, its morning journey was a month and its evening journey was a month. He said: It was mentioned to me that there was a house on the bank of the Tigris in which was written a letter written by some of Solomon’s companions, either from the jinn or from mankind: We have settled it and we did not build it, and we found it built. We went out from Istakhr and said it, and we are returning from it, God willing, so we will spend the night in Syria. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And to Solomon We subjected the wind, its morning journey being a month and its evening journey being a month, he said: He had a wooden ship, and on it were a thousand corners, in each corner a thousand chambers in which the jinn and humans rode, under each corner a thousand devils, they and the winds would raise that ship, and when it was lifted the wind would come gently and move with it, and they would move with it. He would take a nap with a people who were a month apart from him, and he would spend the evening with a people who were a month apart from him, and the people would not know until the armies and soldiers had shaded them with him. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Amir told us: Qara told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, Its morning is a month and its evening is a month, he said: He would go out in the morning and take a nap in Istakhr, then he would come back from there, and its evening would be in Kabul. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Hammad told us, he said: Qurra told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, similarly. And his saying, And We made a spring of molten copper flow for him, means: We melted a spring of copper for him and made it flow for him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We caused a spring of molten copper to flow for him. The spring of copper was in the land of Yemen, and today only what God brought forth for Solomon is of benefit. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We made a spring of molten copper flow for him, he said: The molten copper flowed as water flows, and it was worked with as dough was worked with milk. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We made a spring of molten copper flow for him, meaning: copper. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We made a spring of molten copper flow for him, meaning: the spring of copper flowed. And His statement, And among the jinn are those who work in his presence by permission of their Lord, God Almighty says: And among the jinn are those who obey him, take his orders, and abide by his prohibitions, so they do what he commands in his presence in obedience to him by permission of their Lord. He says: By God’s command to do that, and His making it subservient to him. And whoever among them deviates from Our command, He says: And whoever among the jinn slips and turns away from Our command which We commanded of obeying Solomon, We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blazing Fire, in the Hereafter, and that is the punishment of the blazing fire of Hell. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And whoever among them deviates from Our command meaning, whoever among them turns away from Our command from what Solomon commanded him to do, We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze.
34:13: He, the Most High, means: The jinn made for Solomon whatever he wanted of niches, which is the plural of niche. The niche is the front of every mosque, house, and prayer place. From this is the saying of Adi bin Zaid: Like ivory dolls in the sanctuaries or like eggs in a garden, its flower is illuminated. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, whatever He wills of sanctuaries, he said: Buildings less than palaces. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They make for him whatever he wishes of sanctuaries and palaces and mosques. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, They make for him whatever he wills of sanctuaries, he said: The sanctuaries are the dwellings. And he recited the statement of God, The angels called to him while he was standing praying in the sanctuary (Al Imran 3:39). Amr bin Abdul Hamid Al-Amili told me: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: They make for him whatever he wishes of sanctuaries. He said: The sanctuaries are the mosques. His saying, and statues, means that they make statues of him from copper and glass. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And statues, he said: of copper. Bishr told us, he said: Yazij told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And statues, he said: Of glass and the like. Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us: Marwan told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding God’s statement, And statues, he said: Pictures. His saying, And basins like wells, means: And they carve out for him whatever basins he wants, which are like wells. It is the plural of jabiyah, and jabiyah is the basin from which water is collected, as Al-A’sha Maymun ibn Qays said: Go to the Al-Muhallaq Club, a plate of Sheikh Al-Iraqi’s money, and you’ll be surprised As the other said: It became a collector of cisterns as if it were the skin of the sky outside. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, and basins like wells, meaning: like a well on the ground. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, and basins like cisterns, meaning by cisterns: basins. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And basins like basins. He said: Like basins. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and basins like watering cans, he said: the watering places for camels. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And basins like wells. He said: Basins like a well of earth made of bone, and a well of earth: water collects in it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, and basins like basins, like basins. Amr told us, he said: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, he said: Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And basins like basins. He said: Like camel basins made of bone. His saying, and fixed pots, means: fixed pots that cannot be moved from their places, nor shifted due to their size. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and pots fixed on the ground, he said: bones. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And pots fixed firmly in the ground, he said: Bones fixed in the ground that do not move from their places. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, and fixed pots, he said: The example of the mountains is their size, food is made in them from the size and bulk, they do not move, nor are they transported, just as He said of the mountains: fixed. And His statement, Work, O family of David, in gratitude, God Almighty says: And We said to them, “Work in obedience to God, O family of David, in gratitude to Him for the blessings He has bestowed upon you, with which He has singled you out from among all of His creation, along with gratitude to Him for the rest of His blessings that He has bestowed upon you along with all of His creation.” And He left out the mention of And We said to them, being satisfied with the indication of the speech to what He left out of it. And He extracted His statement, in gratitude, as a source from His statement, Work, O family of David, because the meaning of His statement, Work, is to thank your Lord by obeying Him, and that working in what pleases God is gratitude to God. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Musa bin Ubadah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, regarding his statement, Work, O family of David, in gratitude. He said: Gratitude is fear of God and working in obedience to Him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Haywah told me, on the authority of Zuhrah ibn Ma’bad, that he heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli say: Work, O family of David, in gratitude. And the best gratitude is praise. He said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Work, O family of David, in gratitude, he said: He gave you and taught you and subjected to you what He did not subject to others, and He taught you the language of birds. Be grateful to Him, O family of David. He said: Praise is a part of gratitude. And His statement, And few of My servants are grateful, God Almighty says: And few of My servants are sincere in their belief in My Oneness, and are devoted to My obedience and gratitude for My blessings upon them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And few of My servants are grateful, meaning: Few of My servants are monotheists in their monotheism.
34:14: God Almighty says: So when We carried out Our decree upon Solomon, that he should die, and he died, “what indicated to them his death means: The jinn did not indicate Solomon’s death except a creature of the earth which is a termite that fell upon his staff, which he was leaning upon, and ate it. This is what God Almighty says: ate his staff. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna and Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Except for a creature of the earth that eats away at his staff, meaning: the termite eats away at his staff. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, It eats his staff, he said: His stick. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told me, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Except for the creature of the earth, he said: the termite. It eats his staff, he said: his stick. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Abdullah bin Musa told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, It eats his staff, he said: His stick. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Uthma told us: Saeed bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, It ate his staff, it ate his staff until it fell. Musa bin Harun told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Al-Mansa’ah is the stick in the language of the Abyssinians. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Al-Mansa’ah is the stick. The reciters differed in their recitation of his saying Mansatuhu. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the people of Basra recited it as Mansatuhu without a hamza. The one who found fault with the reciter of that from the people of Basra claimed that the mansat is the stick, and that its origin is from Nasa’at bihi al-Ghanam. He said: It is from the hamza that the Arabs left, just as they left the hamza of the word al-Nabi, al-Bariyah, and al-Khabiyah. And he recited a verse by some poets about leaving the hamza in that: If you step on the mantle of old age, then fun and flirting have become distant from you. Al-Farra’ reported on the authority of Abu Jaafar Al-Rawasi that he asked Abu Amr about it, and he said mansata without a hamza. The majority of Kufan readers read it as mansa’atu with a hamza, as if they attributed that to the fact that it is a passive participle, from nasat al-ba’ir meaning to urge a camel on so that it will walk faster, just as one says nas’at al-laban meaning to pour water on it, which is an-nasi’. And as one says nas’a God fi ‘ajalak meaning may God prolong your life. Abu Jaafar said: They are two readings, and each one of them has been read by scholars among the reciters with one meaning. So whichever one the reciter reads, he is correct, although I choose the hamza in it because it is the original. And His statement, So when he fell down, the jinn realized God Almighty says: So when Solomon fell down in defeat, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen which they claim to know they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment for a full year after Solomon’s death, while they thought that Solomon was alive. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated: Musa ibn Mas`ud Abu Hudhayfah narrated: Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated: `Ata` ibn al-Sa`ib narrated: Sa`id ibn Jubayr narrated: Ibn `Abbas narrated: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whenever Solomon, the Prophet of God, would pray, he would see a tree growing in front of him. He would say to it, ‘What is your name?’ It would say, ‘So-and-so.’ He would say, ‘You are nothing.’ If it was planted, it would be planted, and if it was used for medicine, it would be written down. While he was praying one day, he saw a tree in front of him. He said to it, ‘What is your name?’ It said, ‘The carob tree.’ He said, ‘What are you for?’ It said, ‘For the destruction of this House.’ So Solomon said, ‘O God, conceal my death from the jinn so that mankind may know that the jinn do not know the unseen.’ So he carved it into a staff and leaned on it for a year while the jinn were working. But the termites ate it, and he fell down. It became clear to mankind that if the jinn knew the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating torment for a year.” He said: Ibn `Abbas used to recite it like this. He said: So the jinn thanked the termites. She used to bring her water. Musa bin Harun narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned on the authority of Abu Malik, and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Marra Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Solomon used to spend a year or two years in the Holy House, and a month or two months, and less than that and more, bringing his food and drink. He entered it on the occasion that he died, and that was because there was not a day in which he woke up without a tree growing on it, and he would ask it, ‘What is your name?’ The tree would say, ‘My name is such and such.’ He would say to it, ‘Why did it grow?’ It would say, ‘It grew for such and such.’ He would order it to be cut down. If it grew for planting, he would plant it, and if it grew for medicine, it would say, ‘It grew for medicine for such and such.’ He would make it like that, until a tree grew called Al-Kharuba. He asked it, ‘What is your name?’ It said to him, ‘I am Al-Kharuba.’ He would say, ‘Why did it grow?’ It said, ‘To destroy this mosque.’ Solomon said, ‘What was God like?’” To destroy it while I am alive, you are the one upon whose face is my destruction and the destruction of the Holy House. So he took it off and planted it in his wall, then he entered the sanctuary, and stood praying leaning on his staff, and he died without the devils knowing about it, and they worked for him, fearing that he would come out and punish them. The devils used to gather around the sanctuary, and the sanctuary had windows in front of it and behind it, and the devil who wanted to take it off would say: Are you not a skin if you enter? So I came out from the other side, and one of those devils entered and passed by, and no devil looked at Solomon in the sanctuary except that he burned, so he passed by and did not hear the voice of Solomon, peace be upon him, then he returned and did not hear, then he returned and fell in the house and did not burn, and he saw that Solomon had fallen, so he went out and told the people that Solomon had died, so they opened it and took him out and found his staff, which is the staff in the Ethiopian language, that the termites had eaten it, and they did not know how long he had died, so they put the termites on the staff, and it ate from it for a day and a night, then they calculated in that manner and found that he had died a year ago. And in the reading of Ibn Mas`ud: So they continued to strive for him after his death for a full year. Then the people became certain that the jinn had been lying to them, and if they had known the unseen, they would have known of Solomon’s death, and they would not have remained in the torment for a year working for him. This is the saying of God: “Nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth that gnawed at his staff. So when he fell down, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.” He says: Their matter became clear to the people that they had been lying to them. Then the devils said to the termite: If you were eating food, we would have brought you the best food, and if you were drinking drink, we would have given you the best drink, but we will transfer water and clay to you. So what is inside the wood is what the devils bring to it as thanks for it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The jinn used to tell mankind that they knew things of the unseen, and that they knew what would happen tomorrow. So they were tested by the death of Solomon, so he died and remained on his staff for a year, and they were not aware of his death, and they were subjected to that year, working diligently. So when he came out, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment. And they had remained diligently and working for him for a year. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff, he said: Solomon said to the Angel of Death: O Angel of Death, when you command me, inform me. He said: So he came to him and said: O Solomon, I have commanded you, you have only a short time left. So he called the devils and they built over him a palace of glass, with no door. So he stood up to pray and leaned on his staff. He said: Then the Angel of Death entered upon him and took his soul while he was leaning on his staff, and he did not do that to escape from the Angel of Death. He said: And the jinn were working in front of him and looking at him, thinking that he was alive. He said: Then God sent a creature of the earth. He said: A creature that eats sticks and is called Al-Qadih. It entered it and ate it, until it ate the inside of the stick, it weakened and became heavy for it, so it fell dead. He said: When the jinn saw that, they dispersed and left. That is what His statement, Nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. He said: The stick is the mansa’ah. Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: Solomon, son of David, was praying. He died while he was praying, and the jinn were working, unaware of his death, until the termites ate away at his staff, and he fell down. And in His statement, If they had is in the nominative case because it was made clear, because the meaning of the statement is: When he fell down, it became clear and was revealed, that if the jinn had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment. As for the interpretation that Ibn Abbas interpreted, that it means: the jinn and mankind became clear, then it should be in the accusative case by repeating it to the jinn, and likewise according to this reading the jinn should be in the accusative case, except that I do not know of any of the reciters of the regions who read the jinn in the accusative case, and if it were in the accusative case then in his saying the jinn became clear there would be a pronoun for the mention of mankind.
34:15: God Almighty says: There was for the children of Sheba in their dwelling place a clear sign and a clear proof that they had no Lord except the One who bestowed upon them the blessings they had. Saba is the name of Abu Al-Yaman, according to the Messenger of God. Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki` narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Kalbi, on the authority of Yahya ibn Hani`, on the authority of Urwah al-Muradi, on the authority of a man among them called Furwah ibn Masik, who said: “I said, ‘O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, tell me about Saba’. Was it a man, a woman, a mountain, or animals?’ He said, ‘No, he was an Arab man who had ten sons. Six of them were considered auspicious and four were considered unlucky. As for those who were considered auspicious from him, they were Kindah, Himyar, Azd, the Ash`ariyyun, Madhhij, and Anmar, from whom came Khatham and Bajila. As for those who were considered unlucky, they were `Amilah, Judham, Lakhm, and Ghassan.” Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan bin Al-Hakam narrated to us, saying: Abu Sabrah Al-Nakha’i narrated to us, on the authority of Furwah bin Masik Al-Qat’i, who said: “A man said: O Messenger of God, tell me about Saba’, what is it? A land or a woman? He said: It is neither a land nor a woman, but a man who gave birth to ten children, six of whom were on the right and four on the left. As for those who were on the wrong, they were Lakhm, Judham, Amla, and Ghassan. As for those who were on the right, they were Kinda, Al-Ash’ariyyun, Al-Azd, Madhhij, Himyar, and Anmar. A man said: Who are Anmar? He said: Those from whom are Khatham and Bajila.” Abu Kurayb narrated: Al-Anqazi narrated: Asbat bin Nasr informed me, on the authority of Yahya bin Hani’ Al-Muradi, on the authority of his father, or on the authority of his uncle Asbat is uncertain, who said: “Farwa bin Masik came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘O Messenger of God, tell me about Saba’, was it a mountain or a land?’ He said: ‘It was neither a mountain nor a land, but rather a man from the Arabs who gave birth to ten tribes.’ Then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: ‘And Anmar, who say that they are from Bajila and Khatham.’ So if the matter is as narrated from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that Saba’ was a man, then the pronunciation and non-pronunciation are moderate. As for the pronunciation, it is the name of a well-known man, and as for leaving the pronunciation, it is the name of a tribe or a land. And scholars among the reciters have recited each of them.” The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase in their dwellings. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it in their dwellings in the plural, meaning the dwellings of the family of Saba. The majority of the Kufic reciters read it in their dwelling in the singular and with a kasra on the kaf, which is the language of the people of Yemen as far as I was told. Hamza read it their dwelling in the singular and with a fatha on the kaf. The correct statement regarding this matter, in our view, is that all of these readings have similar meanings, so whichever one recites them, he is correct. We have already explained the meaning of his statement, a sign. As for his statement, two gardens on the right and on the left, he means two gardens between two mountains, on the right and left of whoever approaches them. Their description, as mentioned to us, was as follows: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us: I heard Qatada, regarding His statement, There was for Sheba in their dwelling place a sign - two gardens on the right and on the left, he said: There were two gardens between two mountains, and a woman would take out her bucket on her head and walk between two mountains, and her bucket would fill up without her hand touching it. But when they transgressed, God sent against them a creature called Jarth, which dug into them and drowned them, and nothing remained for them except tamarisk and a few lote trees. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement, There was certainly for Sheba in their dwelling place a sign - two gardens on the right and on the left... to the statement, But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of the dam, he said: Not a single mosquito, fly, flea, scorpion, or snake was seen in their city. Even though caravans would come with lice and insects on their clothes, they would have no sooner looked at their homes than the insects would die. He said: Even though a person would enter two gardens, he would hold a basket over his head, and when he came out, that basket would be full of all kinds of fruit, but he had not taken anything from it with his hand. He said: And the dam watered it. The two gardens were raised in His statement, Two gardens on the right and on the left, as a translation of the sign, because the meaning of the statement is: There was certainly for Sheba in their dwelling place a sign - two gardens on their right and on their left. And His statement, Eat of the provision of your Lord, which He provides for you from these two gardens, from their crops and fruits, and be grateful to Him, for what He has bestowed upon you from His provision. And this is the end of the report. Then the report about the town began, and it was said: This is a good town, meaning it is not a salt marsh, but as we mentioned about its description from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, that it was as Ibn Zayd described it, that there was nothing harmful in it, wild animals, creeping things, or insects. And a Forgiving Lord, he says: And a Forgiving Lord of your sins if you obey Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, A good land and a Forgiving Lord, and your Lord is Forgiving of your sins, a people to whom God has given a blessing, and commanded them to obey Him, and forbade them from disobeying Him.
34:16: God Almighty says: So Sheba turned away from obeying her Lord and turned away from following what her messengers had called her to, that He is her Creator. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, he said: God sent thirteen prophets except for Saba, but they denied them. So We sent upon them the flood of the dam. God Almighty says: So We pierced their shores when they turned away from believing in Our messengers, with a flood that used to hold back the floods from them. The dam is the well that holds back water. Its singular is dam, and it is what Al-A’sha meant when he said: In that there is a model for the follower and a destination that has been forgotten by the dam. Rajam bint Hamir has donkeys. When their water comes, he does not throw up. The Aram was mentioned as one of the things that Bilqis built. Who said that? Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Dawraqi narrated to us, saying: Wahb bin Jarir narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: I heard Al-Mughirah bin Hakim say: When Bilqis became king, her people started fighting over the water of their valley. She kept forbidding them, but they would not obey her, so she gave up her kingdom and went to her palace and left them. When evil increased between them and they regretted it, they came to her and wanted her to return to her kingdom, but she refused. They said: You must return or we will kill you. She said: You do not obey me, and you do not have minds, and you will not obey me. They said: We will obey you, and we have not found any good in us after you. So she came and ordered that their valley be blocked by a wall. Ahmad said, Wahb said, my father said: I asked Al-Mughirah bin Hakim about Al-Aram, and he said: It is in the words of Himyar Al-Masnat. It blocked the space between the two mountains, so it held back the water from behind the dam, and made for it gates, one above the other, and built a huge pool behind it, and made in it twelve outlets for their rivers. When the rain came, the torrent was held back from behind the dam, so I ordered the upper gate to be opened, and its water flowed into the pool, and I ordered the dung to be thrown into it, and some of the dung came out faster than others. So those rivers continued to narrow, and the dung was sent into the water, until it all came out together, and it was divided between them according to that, until what happened to her and Solomon happened. Ahmad bin Omar Al-Basri told us: Abu Saleh bin Zuraiq told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, regarding his statement, So We sent upon them the flood of the dam, he said: Al-Masnat in the Yemeni dialect. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, The flood of the dam, he said: severe. And it was said that the dam is the name of a valley belonging to these people. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then We sent upon them the flood of the dam, he said: It was a valley in Yemen, which flowed to Mecca, and they were given water and their flood would end there. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, So We sent upon them the flood of the dam. It was mentioned to us that the flood of the dam was a valley into which streams from various valleys gathered, so they deliberately blocked up the space between the two mountains with pitch and stones, and made gates over it. They would take from its water what they needed, and block off from them whatever part of its water they did not need. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, Then We sent upon them the flood of Al-Arim, that it was a valley called Al-Arim, and whenever it rained, the valleys of Yemen would flow into Al-Arim, and the water would gather around it. So the Sabaeans went to Al-Arim and blocked the space between the two mountains, and they blocked it with rocks and tar, and it was blocked for a period of time, with no hope of water. He said: They were not afraid. Others said: Al-Aram is an attribute of the land they had, not its name. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, The flood of the dam, meaning: the severe one. The reason that caused God to send that flood upon them, as he mentioned to me, was a rat that God sent against their dam, and it made a hole in it. Then the scholars differed about the description of what happened in that hole, which led to the destruction of their two gardens. Some of them said: The description of that was that when the flood found work in the dam, it worked in it, then the water overflowed onto their gardens, drowning them and destroying their land and their homes. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: They, meaning the Sabaeans, had a dam that they had built as an everlasting structure, and it was what would prevent a flood from reaching their property. It was claimed in their knowledge of their divination that only a mouse could destroy their dam, so they did not leave a crack between two rocks without tying a cat to it. When the time came, and God intended for them to drown, as they say, a red mouse approached one of those cats and harassed it until it was behind it, meaning the cat. It entered the gap that was near it and penetrated the dam, digging in it until it weakened for the flood, and they did not know. When the flood came, it found a hole, so it entered it until it pulled out the dam and flooded the money, carrying it away until nothing remained of it except what God mentioned. When they dispersed, they went to the divination of Imran bin Amir. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: When the people abandoned God’s command, God sent upon them a rat called Al-Khald, which pierced their bottom until it flooded their gardens and destroyed their land as punishment for their deeds. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: When they transgressed and rebelled, meaning Saba, God sent a rat against them, which breached the dam on them, and God drowned them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: God sent a rat against them, and gave it power over those who had been holding back the water that was used to irrigate them, so it destroyed the mouths of those stones, and everything in them of lead and other things, until it left them as stones. Then God sent the flood of the dam, and it uprooted that dam and what it had been holding back, and it uprooted those two gardens, and took them away. He recited: So We sent upon them the flood of the dam and replaced their two gardens with two gardens. He said: It took away those villages and the two gardens. Others said: The reason for that was that the water they used to fill their gardens flowed to a place other than the place they used to benefit from, and as a result their gardens were ruined. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God sent upon them - meaning upon the dam - a beast from the earth, and it made a hole in it, and that water flowed to a place other than the place from which they had benefited, and God replaced their two gardens with two gardens of bitter food, and that was when they disobeyed and were arrogant in their living. The first statement is more similar to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation, as God Almighty mentioned that He sent the flood of the dam upon them, and that sending it upon them would not have happened except by pouring it upon them, or upon their gardens and their land, not by diverting it from them. And His statement, And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens of bitter fruit, God Almighty says: And We replaced their orchards of fruits with gardens of the harvest of the arak fruit, and the arak is the bitter fruit. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God replaced their two gardens with bitter fruit, and bitter fruit is the arak tree. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: I heard Al-Hasan say, regarding His statement, My beings eat bitter fruit, he said: I think he said: bitter fruit is the arak tree. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Abdullah bin Musa told me, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, He ate Khamt. He said: Khamt is the arak tree. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, My own food is bitter, he said: the arak. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: My self eats fermented fruit. And fermented fruit is the arak tree, and its food is the barberry tree. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens of bitter fruit, that God replaced them with gardens of fruits and grapes, as their gardens became bitter, which is the arak tree. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens, he said: I will take away those towns and gardens and replace for them what I told you with bitter food. He said: The bitter is the arak tree. He said: He replaced the grapes with arak, and the fruit with tamarisk, and some of the few lote trees. The reciters differed in their recitation of this word. The majority of reciters in the regions read it with the tanween of akal, except for Abu Amr, who adds it to khamat, meaning: those with khamat fruit. As for those who did not add that to khamat, and added the tanween to akal, they considered khamat to be the food, so they returned it to it in its i'rab. The reciters of the regions read it with the damma of the alif and the kaf of akal, except for Nafi', who used to lighten it. The correct reading in my opinion is the reading of those who read it as dhawati akal with a damma on the alif and the kaf due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on this, and with the tanween of akal due to the widespread reading in that way among the reciters of the regions, without seeing any error in the reading of those who read it by adding it to the khamt. This is in adding it and not adding it, similar to the Arabs’ saying in the garden of so-and-so: An’ab karem and An’ab karem. Sometimes they add the an’ab to the karem because it is from it, and sometimes they add the tanween, then they translate it as karem because the grapes are the fruit of the vine. As for the tamarisk, it is called tarfa’. It is also said that it is a tree similar to the tamarisk, except that it is larger than it. It is also said that it is the samr. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And tamarisk, he said: tamarisk is the tamarisk tree. And his saying, And some few lote trees, means: My food is bitter gourd, tamarisk, and some few lote trees. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: My own food is bitter fruit and tamarisk and a little lote tree. He said: While the tree of the people was the best of trees, God made it one of the worst trees because of their deeds.
34:17: And His statement, That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief, the Most High says: This that We did to these people of Sheba, by sending upon them the flood of the dam, until their wealth was destroyed and their gardens were ruined, was a recompense from Us for their disbelief in Us and their denial of Our messengers. And that in His statement, That is how We recompensed them is in the accusative case because of the occurrence of We recompensed them for it, and the meaning of the statement is: We recompensed them for that because they disbelieved. And his saying, And shall We reward anyone but the ungrateful? The reciters differed in their recitation of it. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, recited it as and shall We reward with a ya and opened the zay as if the subject was not named, except the ungrateful in the nominative case. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as and shall We reward with a noon and with a kasra on the zay “except the ungrateful” in the accusative case. The correct statement about this is that they are two well-known readings among the reciters of the regions, and they are close in meaning, so whichever one recites it, the reciter is correct. The meaning of the statement is: Thus did We reward them for their disbelief in God. And who is rewarded except the ungrateful for the blessings of God? If someone were to say: Does God not reward those who believe in Him for their righteous deeds, specifically rewarding those who disbelieve? It would be said: Is anyone rewarded except the ungrateful? It would be said: The recompense in this case is the recompense, and God, the Exalted, promised the people of faith in Him that He would bestow His favor upon them, and that He would reward them for one of their righteous deeds ten times as much, to an endless multiplication. And He promised the sinner among His servants that He would bestow the same amount of bad deeds on them for one of their sins, as a reward for their crime. The reward is for the people of major sins and disbelief, and the recompense is for the people of faith along with His favor. That is why He, the Most High, said in this case: And does He reward except the ungrateful? It is as if He, the Most High, said: No one is rewarded, no one is rewarded for his deeds except the ungrateful, since the reward is like the one for whom he is rewarded, and God does not forgive him any of his sins, nor does He erase any of them in this world. As for the believer, He bestows His favor upon him as I have described. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And shall We reward? means shall We punish. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief. And do We recompense except the ungrateful?” When God the Almighty intends to honor a servant, He accepts his good deeds, and when He intends to humiliate a servant, He withholds his sins until he meets him on the Day of Resurrection. He said: “It was mentioned to us that a man was on a road in Madinah when a woman passed by him. He followed her gaze until he came to a wall and his face was wounded. He came to the Prophet of God while his face was flowing with blood and said: O Prophet of God, I did such and such. The Prophet of God said to him: When God the Almighty intends to honor a servant, He hastens his punishment for his sin in this world, and when He intends to humiliate a servant, He withholds his sins until he meets him on the Day of Resurrection as if he were a tailless donkey.”
34:18: God Almighty says, informing us of His blessings that He bestowed upon these people who wronged themselves: And We placed between their land and the towns which We had blessed, which are the Levant, towns visible. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The towns which We have blessed, he said: Ash-Sham. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed meaning the Levant. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, The towns which We have blessed, he said: the Levant. It was said: It refers to the villages in which the Holy House was blessed. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed, towns visible. He said: The land which We had blessed is the Holy Land. And His saying, towns visible, means: connected towns, and they are Arab towns. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ya'qub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja', he said: I heard Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, And We placed between them and the towns which We have blessed, towns visible, he said: Towns that were connected. He said: One of them would go out in the morning and take a nap in one town, and in the evening he would take shelter in another town. He said: A woman would place her basket on her head, then spin her spindle, and not come back until it was full of all the fruits. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Apparent villages means continuous. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, visible villages means: Arab villages between Medina and the Levant. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told me, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, villages visible, he said: the Sarawat. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, villages apparent, meaning: Arab villages, and they are between Medina and Ash-Sham. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed, towns visible, he said: There were towns visible between their town and Ash-Sham. He said: A woman would go out with her spindle and her axe on her head, going from one town to the next, and she would be seen in a town carrying neither provisions nor water because of the distance between her and Ash-Sham. And His statement, And We have determined therein the journey, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: And We have made between their towns and the towns which We have blessed a measured journey, from house to house, and from town to town. They do not stop except in one town, and they do not go out except from one town. And His saying, Travel therein, nights and days, in security. He says: And We said to them, Travel in these towns, between your towns and the towns which We have blessed, nights and days, in security, not fearing hunger or thirst, nor injustice from anyone. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “Travel therein in peace by night and by day,” they do not fear injustice or hunger, but they go out in the morning and take a nap, and they come back in the evening and spend the night in a village of people with a garden and a river, until it was mentioned to us that a woman would put her basket on her head and scoop it with her hand, and her basket would be full of fruit before she returned to her family without her having picked anything, and a man would travel without carrying with him provisions or a water skin from what had been spread out for the people. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, and days of security, he said: There is no fear in them.
34:19: The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement "Our Lord, extend between our journeys. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it as Our Lord, extend between our journeys" as a supplication and a question with the letter alif. Some of the people of Mecca and Basra read it as "ba'd" with a shaddah on the 'ayn as a supplication as well. It was reported from the earlier scholars that they used to read it as "Our Lord, extend between our journeys" as a statement from God that God did that to them. It was reported from another that he read it as "Our Lord, ba'd" as a statement as well, except that the Lord is the vocative. The correct reading for this according to us is Our Lord, keep away and after because these are the two readings known in the reading of the regions, and what is other than them is not known among them. However, the interpretation of the people of interpretation also confirms the reading of the one who reads it as a supplication and a question, and this also increases the other reading’s distance from correctness. If this is the correct reading, then the interpretation of the statement is: “They said: O our Lord, extend our journeys, and place between us and Syria deserts and wildernesses, so that we may ride our camels therein and take provisions with us therein.” This is evidence of the people’s arrogance towards God’s blessing and kindness to them, and their ignorance of the extent of well-being. Their Lord hastened the answer to them, just as He hastened to those who said: If this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. He gave them what they desired and asked for from the question. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Hasin told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding this verse: And they said, ‘Our Lord, extend between our journeys.’ He said: They had villages connected to Yemen, some of which looked towards others, so they became arrogant about that and said: Our Lord, extend between our journeys. He said: So God sent upon them the flood of the dam, and made their food tamarisk, khutmah, and some few lote trees. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding His statement, And they said, ‘Our Lord, lengthen between our journeys.’ And they wronged themselves. He said: For they were arrogant in their lives and said, If the fruit of our gardens were further away than they are, it would be more fitting for us to desire it. So they were torn between Ash-Sham and Saba’ and their two gardens were exchanged for two gardens of bitter fruit and tamarisk, and some few lote trees.
